key_insight: FDE-Gym shifts agent evaluation from clean, fully specified benchmarks to the messier reality of customer delivery, where success depends on clarifying vague requirements and operating in live systems. It provides a realistic testbed for measuring how well AI agents handle end-to-end delivery work, not just scripted tasks.
problem_solved: Current agent benchmarks often assume the task is already fully defined, but real forward-deployed engineering work is ambiguous, iterative, and constrained by real customer environments. This paper addresses the gap between benchmark performance and practical delivery performance.
method: Built FDE-Gym, a benchmark with 95 end-to-end delivery tasks drawn from 20 customer scenarios across 18 industries.
Adapted tasks from real-world delivery projects with help from industry experts to preserve ambiguity and operational realism.
Evaluates agents in simulated customer delivery settings where they must infer requirements, handle live-system constraints, and uncover hidden assumptions.
impact: For AI practitioners, FDE-Gym offers a more realistic way to test whether agents can actually deliver useful outcomes in production-like settings. It can help identify weaknesses in planning, requirement clarification, and tool use before deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing the delivery workflow from ambiguous request to completed solution
Comparison chart contrasting traditional benchmarks vs. FDE-Gym realism
Industry coverage map or grid showing 20 scenarios across 18 sectors
Icons for ambiguity, live systems, constraints, and customer communication
paper_title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
paper_authors: Dongxu Yang, Hongda Yan, Renxin Wang, Baoli Zhang, Haojia Zuo
